articles.headline: Breeders’ Cup 2026, day two: horse racing – live
keyFacts: Japanese horse T O Elvis won the Sprint on dirt after passing favourite Englishman near the finish line.
Syndicate-owned horse Bacio won the Turf Sprint for trainer Wesley Ward.
European runner Notable Speech will compete next as favourite in the Mile.
body: Aidan O’Brien, True Love’s trainer, also has Puerto Rico in this race, although he’s drawn wide in stall 14. And there’s a couple of Japanese-trained runners too, in Ask Ikigomi and Lugal, and the former has at least an each-way chance on ratings having been edged out by a nose in a Grade One at Tokyo last time.

After the Euro-wobble in the first two races on the card, there could be no better trainer than Charlie Appleby to get the bandwagon rolling again, in a contest where he has a near-perfect record of four wins from five starters.

Notable Speech, last year’s winner, won with something to spare and has looked every bit as good, if not better, so far this year, including when successful in the Grade One Woodbine Mile last time with his leading US-trained rival, Deterministic, in second.

Notable Speech will set off as a short-priced and worthy favourite but faces some stern opposition, including Lake Forest, who runs in the blue-and-white colours of Tony Bloom and will bid to set the seal on a perfect day for the owner of Brighton & Hove Albion after their magnificent victory at Manchester City earlier on.
Lake Forest did not have any luck in running when second over today’s course-and-distance in the Turf Mile last time out.
And there is a Classic winner in the field too, as True Love took the 1,000 Guineas at Newmarket back in May.

There’s no way Englishman was beaten by his draw there, he was just beaten by a better horse on the day. T O Elvis was at least eight lengths adrift when Englishman hit the lead two out, but he showed incredible finishing speed to stay on all the way up the stretch and grab the lead two strides from the line
Liam Smith, meanwhile, did not drop away after being passed and rewarded his each-way backers by staying on well for third.
Now Englishman settles second after a quarter, Liam Smith is leading.
Englishman takes Liam Smith and goes into the lead, he leads by two halfway down the stretch
But here’s T O Elvis for Japan, he trying to chase down the favourite, gaining all the time and YES! he’s got there, T O Elvis is a big winner on the dirt for Japan.

Englishman is a clear form pick but he’s drawn in stall 13 and unlikely to get across to the lead with the speedy Mad House drawn one. T O Elvis, meanwhile, is only two stalls closer to the rail in 11, though he a more of a closer.

It’s a definite stab in the dark, but Liam Smith has posted some useful numbers while moving through the ranks and is well drawn to attack in stall three. At around 25-1 with the British bookies, I’m going to take a small each-way interest.
But before we get to the Mile, there’s another hot favourite looming on the horizon in the shape of Englishman, in the Sprint on the dirt.
Cherie DeVaux’s three-year-old has won three of his four starts this season including a dominant success in the H Allen Jerkens Memorial over seven furlongs at Saratoga last time.
The second-pick in the betting is the Japanese-trained T O Elvis, the winner of his last five starts but not seen out since an impressive success at Churchill Downs in May.
And there’s also an interesting outsider on an upward curve in Peter Miller’s Liam Smith, who has emerged via claimers but posted a very impressive time when successful at Santa Anita last time.

Saturday is not unfolding as European racing fans might have hoped so far, but Notable Speech is up next in the Mile in two races’ time while the Turf will surely go to a visitor – it’s just a question of which one.

Looping back to the Turf Sprint earlier on the card, Bacio is syndicate-owned and Wesley Ward was particularly pleased about that as his daughter-in-law, Caitlin, helped to keep Bacio in his yard when offers came in for him earlier in his career.

There was a lot to the whole story behind him, to me getting him, and then once he started winning, me keeping him. He was a sought after horse, a lot of people were coming in. My daughter-in-law brought me one of the greatest gifts ever, my grandson, Killian, and she put an ownership group together with MyRacehorse in order to keep him here in our stable.
It’s so nice to have thousands of owners in this horse and win the Breeders’ Cup, it’s going to really help our sport.

A big let down for the Europeans, neither Blue Bolt nor Precise was ever travelling with purpose and both were beaten before the final turn. Well done to County Kildare-based Willie McCreery though – his 25-1 outsider Jancis came through to finish third, and best of the Euro runners.
Kathynmarissa was sent off at 5-1 on the local tote, but there was 7-1 and 8-1 on offer with British firms beforehand.

The favourites are having a high old time of it so far at this year’s Breeders’ Cup and the local punters clearly see no reason to change a winning formula. Blue Bolt is now evens, despite her wide draw and the slight question mark over her stamina.

Turf races tend to be run at a steadier pace than on the dirt and there is likely to be only moderate pressure on the lead. Both Blue Bolt and Precise are drawn wide, however, and it is quite possible that one or both will end up stuck wide.

Classic Q, on the other hand, should get a perfect trip either on the lead or just behind the pace and Mark Casse’s runner is my idea of the each-way value in the race if you’re taking the current 33-1 with a British bookie.
19.04 Breeders’ Cup Filly & Mare Turf, Grade One, 1m 1½f

Back to the turf now for what is, from a Eurocentric point-of-view, a fascinating head-to-head between Precise and Blue Bolt, although it could be a little unwise to ignore the US-trained challenge entirely.
Blue Bolt needs little introduction, having won all six of her starts this season including four Group Ones, with Precise among the beaten runners in three of those.
That list includes the Falmouth Stakes at Newmarket in July, when Precise was a couple of lengths away in second.

This is their first meeting at a trip beyond a mile, however, and while Blue Bolt’s stamina has yet to be tested, Precise was an excellent second behind Miss Scott when stepping up to 10 furlongs in the Prix de l’Opera at Longchamp last time.
The main hope for a local success, according to the betting at least, is Chad Brown’s Kathymarissa, the winner of the Flower Bowl Stakes at Belmont last time.

But I was also quite taken with the performance of Classic Q in the Grade One First Lady at Keeneland. It was a narrow win – from another of today’s rivals, Lush Lips, but she was drawn nine and caught wide, and has a much better pitch in stall three today.
She is a 12-1 shot in the early betting on the US tote, but currently a frankly insulting 40-1 with at least one British bookmaker according to Oddschecker.
It took three or four minutes for the judge to separate them there, but it was the favourite, Further Ado, that got it on the nod after a thrilling battle to the wire.
He went off at even money in the end, with OwenAlmighty was a 9-1 shot. BracketBuster, meanwhile, almost lost his jockey at the start and was adrift throughout.

The map includes Forged Steel, who was moderately fancied for this but ruled out earlier in the day. He would have been on or close to the lead, but in his absence, Full Serrano, the likely third-favourite, and Chunk Of Gold should still set a decent clip.

Further Ado will be on the rail in behind, but is likely to have at least four or five ahead of him and at the likely odds, I’d rather be with Bracket Buster to get a smoother trip and take it up in the stretch.

If there’s a weak link on the Breeders’ Cup card, then this is probably it. The Classic is a more inviting target for any dirt horse with a fair chance of getting 10 furlongs, and it feels a little telling that only three of the 10 runners managed a win last time out.

Further Ado, the favourite, offers a line to the form of The Puma, a runner in the Classic at the end of the card, as he was a half-length behind him in the Grade One Pennsylvania Derby at Parx in mid-September.
Bracket Buster also ran at Parx last time, finishing second in the Dirt Mile in September after getting caught on the rail approaching the turn out of the back straight.

So, no greenwash on the turf for the Europeans, but Bacio simply flew home there, setting strong fractions – 21.23sec for the quarter, 43.86sec for the half – but still leaving them for dead in the straight.

Comanche Brave was a little agitated before loading and missed the kick by a length, and while he moved up to mid-division by the turn, his race was as good as over once Bacio had kicked. He ended up in a dead-heat for fourth with Time To Dazzle.

The locals are siding with Wesley Ward to saddle a second winner of this race (he was successful with Golden Pal five years ago). He’s opened up at 8-5 on the tote, with Comanche Brave next in at 5-2.

George Weaver’s Cy Fair is currently the only other runner at single-figure odds on 8-1, and she has a squeak on her best form too but was distinctly disappointing when odds-on for a Grade Two at Kentucky Downs in early September. Shesospicy, meanwhile, is 15-1 for a repeat success.
Bacio simply burned off his rivals in his two races in Britain over the summer and is well drawn to attack in stall three. If he can get clear at the turn, it could be all over.

He is likely to face a fair bit more competition for the lead than he did in Europe, though, and Joe Shiesty could definitely apply some pressure if he breaks well from the outside. If so, Comanche Brave and Billy Loughnane, aboard his only ride on today’s card, will be poised to pounce. O’Brien’s runner travels strongly just off the pace and that could be just what’s required.

We’re on to the turf next, and the most obvious barrier to a European clean sweep on the grass in the form of Wesley Ward’s Bacio. He is already familiar to European racing fans as the winner of both the Palace of Holyroodhouse Handicap at Royal Ascot and the Nunthorpe at York in August.

He’s a very obvious favourite back on his home turf, but Donnacha O’Brien’s Comanche Brave is an equally obvious main market rival after his wins in the July Cup and then the Flying Five at the Curragh.
Bacio and Comanche Brave are the only two runners in the field at single-figure odds, but it would be remiss not to mention last year’s winner, Shisospicy, who is back for a second go.

She’s well drawn in stall two but has not seen a track since finishing seventh at Churchill Downs in May, and has been on the wrong end of several setbacks since her win last year. She was forced to miss some juicy targets in the SaudiArabia and Dubai in the early part of the year due to an infection, apparently as the result of a spider bite, and also had a fever shortly before her intended prep for today’s race at Belmont in September.

That pretty much unfolded entirely as expected: Kerry’s Kiss and R Disaster were forward early with Explora in pursuit, and then Ways And Means breezed through the field as if she’d just joined in. She set off as an even-money shot on the tote.

The pace is likely to be fierce as four or five of the runners have been on or close to the lead after the first quarter-mile in the majority of their recent starts, including R Disaster and Kerry’s Kiss, drawn four and eight respectively, who are most likely to duel for the early lead. Explora too likes to be close to the lead, but may end up three or four wide from her outside stall, while Ways And Means should have a smoother time of it towards the inside.
17.10 Breeders’ Cup Filly & Mare Sprint, Grade One, 7f

The Saturday card kicks off with a sprint that isn’t, by European standards at least, as seven furlongs is past the point where a horse can simply go flat out from the start (a bit like the 400m in athletics, when compared to the 100m or 200m). And it is perhaps no co-incidence that wire-to-wire winners are a rarity.

Nor is there a standout trial event that regularly highlights the winner, although Goodnight Olive took in the BallerinaHandicap at Saratoga before her wins in 2022 and 2023. Ways And Means, the morning-line favourite,was the winner of that contest this year, by nearly six lengths, and is expected to go off favourite today.
She breezed past R Disaster, a rival again today, at the top of the stretch and it is difficult to see Saffie Joseph’s mare reversing the form.

The second-favourite, meanwhile, is the three-year-old Explora, from the Bob Baffert stable. She was beaten at odds-on last time out, but had earlier taken the GradeOneTestStakes at Saratoga, over the same seven-furlong trip as the Ballerina, by five lengths.

Another leading contender to consider is Sweet Azteca, a six-year-old who is unbeaten in four starts this year since a stable-switch to join Richard Baltas. Her latest win, in a Grade Three at Del Mar, still leaves her with something to find to trouble the favourite, though.
Ways And Means is short enough in the betting but I can see her getting a better trip through the race than Explora, who is drawn in stall 11 and could end up three or four wide.

Welcome to the Guardian’s liveblog coverage of the main card at the 2026 Breeders’ Cup in Kentucky, where a strong team from Europe will be bidding for a first-ever clean sweep of the Cup’s turf events and, at the climax of the card, all eyes will be on the Japanese superstar, Forever Young, as he bids to become only the second horse in Breeders’ Cup history to win a second Classic.

Yesterday’s three turf events for juveniles were a complete rout for the visitors, who had the first seven home in both the JuvenileTurfSprint and the JuvenileFilliesTurf, and the 1-2-3 in the JuvenileTurf. The European team also have the favourites for three of today’s four turf races, with the only exception being the Turf Sprint at 17.48, where Wesley Ward’s Bacio is nudging even-money to follow up his wins at Royal Ascot and York earlier in the season.

The highlight of the card for European fans is surely the Turf at 21.36, where a host of the continent’s best middle-distance horses will chase a share of the $5m purse, but Notable Speech is a huge runner too in the Mile (20.20) and the latest face-off between Blue Bolt and Precise in the Filly & Mare Turf (19.04) also promises to be something to savour.

It was an evening for the form horses yesterday, which is probably why I somehow managed to find four of the five winners. That, of course, all-but guarantees a complete blank today, but my picks for the nine races are here just in case, and we will be underway on one of the great racing rollercoasters with the Filly & Mare Sprint at 17.10.

articles.headline: Denny Hamlin Makes Surprising Admission About NASCAR Championship Pressure
keyFacts: Joe Gibbs Racing driver Denny Hamlin won the pole for Sunday's Xfinity 500 at Martinsville Speedway while trailing Kyle Larson by 73 points.
Hamlin told reporters he feels little pressure entering the weekend because expectations are low and Larson is favored to win the championship.
Hamlin will start on the front row at Martinsville ahead of Larson before the championship finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway.
body: Denny Hamlin has spent much of his NASCAR career trying to win the one trophy that has eluded him. Now, with another championship slipping further out of reach, he’s feeling something unexpected.
Relief from the pressure.

The Joe Gibbs Racing veteran enters Sunday’s Xfinity 500 at Martinsville Speedway trailing Kyle Larson by 73 points with only two races remaining in the 2026 Cup Series season. It’s hardly the position Hamlin envisioned after entering the Chase as the top seed.
But rather than allowing the deficit to consume him, Hamlin says the circumstances have changed how he’s approaching the weekend.
“I think it’s the first weekend where there’s truthfully little pressure because I think the expectations are just so low,” Hamlin told reporters Saturday .

For a driver who has spent two decades chasing his first Cup championship, it’s a remarkable admission. And it comes at a track where he might have his best opportunity to make the title race interesting again.
Denny Hamlin Sees Opportunity With Little Left to Lose

Hamlin isn’t pretending his championship chances are better than they look. In fact, he acknowledged that Larson has become such a strong favorite that many people have already made up their minds about the outcome.
“I think that everyone believes that it’s kind of a foregone conclusion [that Larson will win], and I’m not saying that they’re wrong by any means,” Hamlin said.
He also acknowledged reaching a point in his career where simply improving his final position in the standings holds little appeal.
“What is the difference in second in points versus fifth? That just doesn’t really matter to me at this point in my career,” he said.
That perspective changes the stakes at Martinsville.
Hamlin doesn’t need another respectable points finish to validate his season. He needs to give Larson something to worry about before the championship finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway.
“So yeah I think it’s a low-pressure, high-opportunity for the 11 team to go out there and do what we need to do this weekend,” Hamlin said.
Martinsville Gives Hamlin a Chance to Change the Conversation
There are few tracks better suited to a Hamlin comeback than Martinsville.
His six Cup Series victories at the Virginia short track are the most among active drivers. Earlier this season, he led 292 of 400 laps, swept both stages and finished second.
And Saturday offered another encouraging sign: Hamlin won the pole with a lap of 19.226 seconds , putting his No. 11 Toyota on the front row for Sunday’s 500-lap race.
Larson, meanwhile, qualified third.

Hamlin also made clear that he isn’t overlooking what Larson and the No. 5 team have accomplished. He credited their remarkable Chase performance while acknowledging that his own team hasn’t executed as consistently as it did during the regular season.
“We just haven’t executed as good as what we did,” Hamlin said.
The difference is that Hamlin no longer has much reason to race conservatively. With Larson holding a commanding advantage, another solid afternoon might not accomplish much.
A dominant Martinsville performance, however, could change the conversation heading into Homestead.
For once, Hamlin can chase the championship without carrying the expectations that usually come with being one of NASCAR’s leading contenders.

body: Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez attempts to reclaim a portion of the world super middleweight title when he returns to action on Halloween to challenge Christian Mbilli for the WBC's 168-pound belt.

The fight is Canelo’s (63-3-2) second in Saudi Arabia, part of a deal with Riyadh Season. He last fought a year ago, where he lost his undisputed 12-stone title to fellow modern great Terence Crawford.
Despite the time off, Canelo didn’t want to take an easy fight back. The multi-division champion aims to have gold around his waist again by beating the dangerous Mbilli.

"I don’t believe in shortcuts. That’s why I go straight to the champion," Canelo said via Boxing Scene. "I already have that experience. I’ve been a champion many years, and I hope to be a champion again. I want to face the best, and he’s a champion, that’s it."

Mbilli (29-0-1) has 23 knockout wins and took out Maciej Sulecki to become the interim champion. Promoted after Crawford relinquished the belt, his last fight was a draw. Mbilli is ready to prove he’s worthy of being champion against Canelo.
"I’m ready to shock the world," said Mbilli. "I have a big respect for Canelo and all his career. I want to congratulate him for this, but Saturday will be a different story. I’m coming for the win."

articles.headline: Tottenham 2-0 Crystal Palace: Premier League – as it happened
keyFacts: Tottenham led Crystal Palace 1-0 at half-time after Archie Gray scored a header and Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off following a VAR review.
Tottenham secured a comfortable win after dominating possession and taking firm control of the match following the red card.
Tottenham will move up to eighth place with this lead and face upcoming matches against Leeds, Ipswich, Sunderland, and Fulham.
body: Some post-match thoughts from Jan Paul van Hecke: “We created a lot of chances, the red card helped us … we had to be patient because we know they play a low block. We took a while to score the second, could have scored more, but we’re happy.”

“I think it was José Mourinho who pooh-poohed the old saw about not looking at the table until 10 games are done; points are points after all,” writes Gary Naylor. “So many clubs seem to be inconsistent or actually imploding before our very eyes. All that manager churn can’t help – coaches need stability to build confidence.”

Save for one nervy moment when Dwight McNeil got a sight of goal, this was very comfortable for Spurs, who took a firm grip of the game after Mateta’s red card. There will be tougher tests ahead, but Tottenham look like a cohesive team again. Palace, on the other hand, look to be in trouble.
90 mins: A lovely little cameo from Williams-Barnett, jinking through Palace defenders like a spring lamb and squaring for Kudus – who shanks away from an open goal in the Sunday League style.

83 mins: Not much happening now, as Palace fans contemplate that long cross-capital journey home. On which subject, here’s Julian Borrill: “Just looking at London, the longest trip looks like Bromley to Wealdstone at 1hr 54min. But a shout-out to Brentford-Hornchurch at 1hr 24min – all on the District Line.”
81 mins: Another fine stop from Henderson, springing to his left to save Gallagher’s goalbound shot. Palace look like they’re going to need him if they’re to stay out of trouble.
79 mins: Should they hold on to this lead, Tottenham will move up to eighth. Their next four games are Leeds (A), Ipswich (H), Sunderland (A) and Fulham (H) – and then it’s the North London Derby.
76 mins: Kulusevski and Udogie come on, replacing Marmoush and Robertson. Now their injury problems are easing, Spurs’ bench is starting to look quite stacked.

The centre-back has been playing almost as an auxiliary forward in the second half, and he does a decent Harry Kane impression here, stretching to beat two Palace defenders with a header. Henderson saves, it hits the underside of the bar, then bounces in off Van Hecke’s bonce as he falls to the floor.
71 mins: Oof! Robertson plays an instinctive one-two with Marmoush, but his touch then lets him down and he’s forced to try and chip Henderson from an impossible angle, sending the ball behind.
69 mins: A potential Palace breakaway is halted by a handball decision. Still, with 20 minutes to go, the visitors have a route to get a result, which looked unlikely at half-time.
65 mins: Pedro Porro is the latest Spurs player to fire high and wide. A second change from De Zerbi: Conor Gallagher is on, replacing Solanke and allowing Marmoush to push further forward.
63 mins: Marmoush has options to his right, but his pass is poor and cut out by Mitchell – only to then ricochet back towards Henderson, who has to parry it away! Proper pinball stuff at either end.
62 mins: Maybe now, as Kamada’s cross floats across the Spurs box and finds McNeil’s boot – but his well-struck shot is blocked by Solanke. That gives Tottenham the chance to break …
61 mins: Van Hecke has a blast from 30 yards out that isn’t particularly close. At what point do Spurs fans start to get antsy about this slender lead?
59 mins: Two changes for Palace, with Anan Khalaili and midweek scorer Eddie Nketiah replacing Pino and Mingueza. Spurs fans give former Gunner Nketiah a frosty reception.
58 mins: Pino is robbed in midfield and Spurs use the little bit of extra space, Tel finding Solanke whose shot is deflected behind. A tenth corner for the hosts, but it comes to nothing.

56 mins: Jan-Paul van Hecke finds himself in the area and has a shot that’s charged down at close range. Pierre Sage, who sounds to me like a French philosopher, chews on his pipe and ponders some changes.

54 mins: In the first 10 minutes of the second half, the ball has spent about 20 seconds in the Spurs final third. There’s a penalty shout as Fernandes’ shot hits Disasi on the shoulder, but not low enough to interest the VAR.
52 mins: Possession is close to 80-20 in Tottenham’s favour, and the territorial battle must be even more one-sided. The hosts’ latest attack ends when Solanke is penalised for a foul.

50 mins: Solanke is next to have a go, taking down Perro’s cross, swivelling and lashing a shot at goal. It’s central, but Henderson still has to throw up a strong arm to stop the power alone beating him.

46 mins: Tel’s shot is deflected off Richards’ shins for a corner, which is headed out into the path of Fernandes. He drills a shot that is flicked off target by a Palace boot – I think that was heading in.
A half-time change for Spurs, with Pedro Porro replacing the goalscorer, Archie Gray. Not sure if that’s injury-related – Gray was excellent in the first half.
“Re: Mateta. If a player decides to slide in, uncontrolled from behind, with their studs up … c’mon, we’ve all got work in the morning,” writes David Penney.

Spurs end the first half a goal and a man up thanks to Archie Gray’s header, after Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off following a VAR review. The hosts have dominated, but need another goal or two to avoid any second-half nerves.

articles.headline: 2026 Breeders' Cup Classic predictions, horses, odds, time, post positions: Horseracing picks via top expert
keyFacts: Trainer Bill Mott is entering two favorite horses, Sovereignty and Knightsbridge, in the 2026 Breeders' Cup Classic.
Keeneland Race Course in Lexington, Kentucky, will host the race on Saturday at 6:16 p.m. ET.

articles.headline: Sunderland's paradox - San Siro trip amid relegation battle
keyFacts: Sunderland is rock bottom in the Premier League after nine games following a 3-1 defeat by Coventry City.
Captain Granit Xhaka and manager Regis le Bris stated the team is struggling due to numerous unforced defensive errors and mistakes.
Despite their domestic relegation battle, Sunderland is performing well in the Europa League and the Carabao Cup.
body: - Published
When Sunderland were handed a trip to the San Siro to face AC Milan in the Europa League, they must have been relishing the chance to rub shoulders with such heavyweights.

Yet by the time they travel to Italy to take on the Serie A giants on 10 December, they may be more concerned about the Premier League match against Nottingham Forest that comes just three days later.
That is because last season's surprise package following promotion are now one of this campaign's strugglers.
They may be mixing it with illustrious big guns in Europe, but they are staring down the barrel of a relegation fight on the domestic front.
Their 3-1 defeat by Coventry City on Saturday has kept Sunderland rock bottom of the table after nine games.
Their situation could worsen significantly very soon, too.

Before they head to Milan, they face a daunting league programme of Chelsea (home), Aston Villa (away), Tottenham (home), Liverpool (away) and local rivals Newcastle (away), with home European games against Croatia's Dinamo Zagreb and Poland's Jagiellonia Bialystok thrown into the mix.
If they fail to cause some upsets in that run and others towards the bottom of the table pick up points, the Black Cats could be dangerously adrift before their dream trip to Milan.
That is why their game against fellow slow starters Forest could turn out to be more important than the San Siro date.
The last time Sunderland won a Premier League game was against Fulham on 30 August - two days after the Europa League league phase draw, and a visit to Milan, was confirmed.

While celebrating that victory and scouring for flights and hotels for their European adventure, surely Sunderland fans did not expect they would be heading into November having not won since in the league.
Including an opening-weekend defeat by Ipswich, they have suffered six defeats with two draws.
"Very disappointed," said captain Granit Xhaka following the Coventry loss.
"We are not doing the things that we have been speaking about; we are not doing the things that we are doing in training. Again, so many mistakes. We have no chance to win any games like this."
European wins, but at a cost?
Yet in Europe, all is well for the Black Cats.
They are ninth in that table, with only goal difference keeping them out of the top eight and a passage directly to the last-16 stage. They have two wins and a draw from their three games.
And in the Carabao Cup, a 3-2 win over Brentford in midweek has set up a quarter-final against fellow league strugglers Crystal Palace.

Yet they have picked up just a point in their three league games that have followed European outings this season, while this defeat against Coventry came on the back of the midweek victory over the Bees in the EFL Cup.
"Football isn't one day good, one day bad," said Xhaka.
"We didn't have [European football] last season. When we lost once last season we came back, but we are doing so many simple mistakes, and if you do mistakes in this league you get punished.
"And we are getting punished every weekend. I don't know exactly what the problem is. Is it concentration, is it other things?
"Of course, we are now bottom of the league, but in football you need to think positive. You need to show courage even if you make mistakes when you play, but that's not the case at the moment."
'It's not a question of luck'
The obvious difference this season so far for Sunderland is their leaky defence.
Last term, they had the fourth meanest back line in the division with only champions Arsenal, Manchester City and Brighton conceding fewer goals.
So far this term, only Ipswich Town and Crystal Palace have let in more than Sunderland.
After just nine games last term, Sunderland had won five, drawn two and lost two with just seven goals conceded.
Now they have already had 17 goals against them in nine matches. It took 15 games to get to that number last season.
In Europe, they have conceded just two goals in three games.

They have now made seven errors which have led to goals conceded, with Coventry's opening two on Saturday down to a failure to deal with a cross and then Luke O'Nien losing possession to Taiwo Awoniyi in the build-up to the second.
"Bad result," Sunderland boss Regis le Bris told BBC's Match of the Day.
"Ups and downs, I think, is the summary of this game and the season so far. We can play good football, and create some good chances, but we also made many unforced errors.
"At this level, especially in the Premier League, the opponent can seize every single opportunity, and [Coventry] did that. It's not a question of luck, it's a question of us."
'We can show our character'
While their defensive errors are clear, Sunderland's efficiency in front of goal may also be catching up with them.

Only relegated Burnley and Wolves had a lower xG difference than Le Bris' side last season. Only three teams - Crystal Palace, Burnley and Wolves - scored fewer than their 42 goals as well, as Sunderland finished with a negative goal difference.
This season they have seven goals in nine, with only second-bottom Forest managing fewer with six.
Sunderland have also missed defender Dan Ballard at the back as he has been out with a hamstring injury since September's international break.
If there are positives to look at, they have faced champions Arsenal, title challengers Manchester City and in-form Brighton already, while earning spirited draws against Brentford and Leeds.
But that may be clutching at straws while bottom of the table.
Qualifying for Europe again seems like a distant dream at the moment.
"It's a difficult position where we are," said Xhaka, "but a situation where we can show our character, show our desire together to come out from here.
"I believe that we can still do it, and let's focus on the next one now."

articles.headline: You asked how Kindle Colorsoft colors look in Dark Mode? The answer might surprise you
keyFacts: Testing showed that the Kindle Colorsoft displays colors in Dark Mode, turning interface borders black while leaving color content untouched.
Amazon confirmed that Colorsoft devices may appear dimmer overall in Dark Mode due to the color E-Ink layer.
Readers can increase front-lit brightness or use an external light source if the screen looks too dim.
body: On my recent unboxing of the brand-new Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition (the one with the brushed aluminum back), I noticed someone asking about the quality of colors in dark mode, and I realized I didn't have a good answer.

Dark Mode, which became popular on modern screens over the past 15 years or so — a throwback to the original CRT displays — has never been my thing. As a result, I don't use it on phones, browsers, or Kindle e-readers. Still, the more I thought about this question (below). The more I wondered about it.
"This might be a dumb question," started one TikTok commenter, "but do the colors still show when in Dark Mode? I've only seen photos in light mode."
I instantly tried to imagine what a comic or graphic novel might look like in Dark Mode and realized I'd never seen it that way either.
Let's try the Colorsoft Dark mode

The Kindle Colorsoft shares a menu system with the rest of the monochrome Kindles, with the Dark Mode option sitting right up top. You access the quick menu with a swipe down from the top of the display. You can also dig into settings to turn on the control from there.

I turned on Dark Mode on the Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition and noticed that my library immediately reversed, turning all the white borders black, but the book, magazine, and graphic novel covers remained untouched. If I opened a book, I saw white text on black pages.
The other thing I noticed is that the screen looked a lot dimmer. Basically, Dark Mode automatically lowers the screen brightness by half.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.

I opened a graphic novel. As with the rest of the Colosoft interface, the borders around each graphic novel page were black. However, each page was still white, with the untouched color panels inside. Honestly, this makes sense, since I can't imagine any artist would want dark mode reversing their work. It would probably look terrible.

I could see all the colors, but the pages looked too dim. Fortunately, I could still push the front-lit LEDs brighter (I turned them up to max) to return some of that vibrancy, though I'm not sure if that defeats the purpose of Dark Mode.

The other option is to take advantage of the Kindle Colorsoft's reflective display (unlike an LCD, there are no traditional backlights). If you have a good external light or even sunlight, the page looks great with or without dark mode, which can reduce eye-straining screen glare and save some battery life (not much of an issue with Kindles).

Here's what I learned: Yes, you can still see colors in Dark Mode, but as Amazon confirmed to me, "When setting Colorsoft devices to dark mode, the screen may appear dimmer overall due to the color E-Ink layer."
If the screen looks too dim, adjust the brightness or find a good light source and enjoy your colorful graphic novels.

articles.headline: 6 Essential Activities GTA Needs to Let Players Experience in Vice City
keyFacts: Polygon published an opinion piece outlining six activities the author hopes GTA 6 will include for players in Vice City.
The suggested activities include learning Spanish, reading on public transportation, becoming an influencer, and going on dates.
The author also expressed a desire for guided city tours and meaningful character progression that reflects player actions.
body: GTA 6 is just around the corner, and despite Rockstar releasing quite a lot of footage over the last month, I still think there's very little to show what we'll actually be doing in the game. Crime, yes. The usual spate of side activities, yes. Having sex, apparently. But there's still a lot of room for speculation about what you can do in those in-between moments. I hope some of these activities make the cut.
1 Learn Spanish

If GTA 6 lets Jason and Lucia become a serious item, then it needs to let me, as Jason, learn Spanish. (That’s assuming that Lucia speaks it, at least a little.) It'd be extremely cute, plus it's kind of mandatory if they're going to share their lives, especially in a place based on Miami, where tons of people speak Spanish. I don't expect Rockstar, or anyone, to put a whole segment of language courses in a non-educational video game, of course. Just a nod to it, maybe, or it could be a passive activity you choose to do and eventually see results from.
2 Read on the bus

Look, I know this isn't an RPG and it's definitely not Persona 5, but when you say "spending time traveling on public transportation," the first thing that comes to mind is reading on the subway. Even if it doesn't improve any kind of stat or have a noticeable benefit, at least it would help Rockstar's efforts at making GTA 6 as realistic as possible. Barring that, I'd settle for listening to the game's radio stations on Jason's or Lucia's phone. With earbuds. Like a civilized human.
3 Become an influencer

GTA side hustles are always a thing, and after seeing Rockstar poke fun at influencer culture in the big Netflix reveal, I do actually think it'd be interesting to play at being an influencer in the game. Turning Jason and Lucia's biggest moments into capital-C Content might not be the smartest idea if you're trying to avoid the law. But surely they can have burner accounts? It sure would be amusing to try and get the perfect framing as you're fighting off civilian vigilantes in the jewelry store, not to mention a potentially clever use of photo mode.
4 Go on dates

Again, if relationships are a big deal in this game, we need to see more of it beyond just the steamy sex scenes. And, y'know, something more romantic than a perfectly planned heist. Maybe a night out at a restaurant or a trip to the cinema or theatre. Is there a cinema in GTA 6? I hope so. Surely Vice City's culture extends beyond strip clubs and drug dens.
5 Take a tour

You can explore the swamps and dive off skyscrapers, sure, but I'd really like a guided tour of Vice City. Seeing the notorious city's efforts at presenting a socially and morally acceptable face seems like the kind of thing GTA would be very good at making fun of, but I'd also like to see something a bit deeper. Say, for example, a guided tour into the history of one of the city's multicultural neighborhoods or even something more lighthearted like a ghost tour. Just something that lets me feel like I'm exploring the city on a deeper level.
6 Have meaningful character progression

Speaking of deeper, it seems like GTA 6 places far greater emphasis on character development than previous installments of the series. That makes me hope there's some kind of progression — beyond just physical appearance — that reflects my actions in the game. Maybe it's just as simple as specializing in one kind of combat over another, but if I'm spending as much time with Jason and Lucia as Rockstar clearly wants me to, there should be something that lets my actions shape that journey in a way different from everybody else. Otherwise, why bother?

articles.headline: Xbox manager says AI is already being used in game development
keyFacts: Xbox strategy manager Brandon Stirrup claimed Xbox uses AI to develop games before deactivating his social media account.
Major studios including Capcom and Epic Games use or plan to use AI, while several independent studios oppose it.
Players and developers cite concerns regarding generative AI, including environmental costs, labor issues, and fears of worker layoffs.
body: Xbox manager says AI is already being used in game development
Brandon Stirrup deleted his comments from X a day after saying that AI usage is widespread in the gaming industry.

Generative AI is one of the most controversial topics in game development right now, and whether it's the future of the medium or a temporary blight on it depends on who you ask. Brandon Stirrup, a strategy manager at Xbox, recently waded into the debate, claiming that Xbox is currently using AI to develop games and those who say they aren't are merely "pretending." Stirrup deactivated his social media account shortly after (though his posts have been archived elsewhere), igniting conversations about what role generative AI actually has or should have in game development.

In some ways, it would be unsurprising to learn that Xbox is using AI to the extent that Stirrup implies. Xbox recently announced the formation of Xbox Labs at least in part as a response to a rising trend of AI-coded game ports; the announcement heavily implied that the new team would use AI as well but didn't say it outright. Xbox owner Microsoft is also a major player in AI development, a fact that's already made Xbox the target of a BDS boycott due to that AI's use by the Israeli military. While Xbox has yet to officially state a position on developing games with AI, other developers are drawing clear lines around where they stand on the practice.
Does everyone really use AI in game development?

Particularly among the largest game studios, there's an insistence that generative AI should be used to speed up game development. Developers including Capcom, Square Enix, Sega, Nexon and Activision have all either used AI in their games or pledged to do so. Fortnite developer Epic Games has been particularly up-front about its AI use, and CEO Tim Sweeney has aggressively promoted it on social media. Multiple game industry studies have also found extremely high adoption rates for AI (around 90 percent), though their limited participant pools and definitions of AI call into question just how representative their responses are.

On the other hand, there are large pockets of the game industry vocally opposed to generative AI. Notably, these tend to be smaller, independent studios without shareholders to impress by touting the cost-savings of AI. These studios include Tunic publisher Finji, Stardew Valley developer ConcernedApe and Clickolding developer Strange Scaffold, among many more. Due to the sheer number and variety of game studios, it's impossible to say just how much of the industry actually uses AI at this point, but claims that "everyone" is using it are clearly false.

There's a similar divide among players about whether generative AI should be embraced or avoided at all costs. While some simply accept AI as part of games going forward, others have pledged to avoid games that use the technology outright due to its environmental costs, labor issues or pure aesthetic preference. That's led to the popularity of tools like a browser extension that makes Steam's AI disclosures more visible and grassroots efforts by developers to implement labels certifying their games as AI-free.
What generative AI actually means for games

The most controversial uses of AI come from generating assets that appear in the final game. Sometimes they're intentionally included, like The Finals' use of AI-generated voices. More commonly, developers claim that art assets found in finished games were meant to be used as placeholders and removed later, as was the case recently with Crimson Desert. Many players and developers alike justify the use of AI in generating code, even if they're opposed to it in other areas.

The effects of AI on game development at large are hard to pin down. While AI can't generate games worth playing without extensive support from skilled developers, there's still fear that executives could use the promise of AI to support laying off workers, and it's still an open question whether AI will ultimately make games easier to develop. One demonstrable trend is the proliferation of low-quality "slop" games, often copying directly from other projects, as seen by the massive increase of AI games in the Steam Next Fest demo event. It's clear that AI is changing the way many games are made, but what those changes actually look like are still to be seen.

articles.headline: Harry Kane in unwanted 14-year first as Borussia Dortmund stun Bayern Munich
keyFacts: Harry Kane missed a penalty as Bayern Munich drew 2-2 with Borussia Dortmund in Der Klassiker on Saturday.
Kane became the first player to miss a penalty in this fixture since Arjen Robben did in April 2012.
Fabio Silva scored a late equalizer for Dortmund to secure the draw after Bayern took the lead through Konrad Laimer.
body: Harry Kane missed a penalty as Bayern Munich dropped points in the 2-2 Der Klassiker draw with Borussia Dortmund.
The newly-crowned Ballon d’Or winner smashed the woodwork with his effort from 12 yards early in the second half at the Allianz Arena with Bayern leading 1-0.
Kane became the first player since Robben in 2012 to miss a penalty during Der Klassiker between Bayern and Dortmund Getty
Kane has only failed to convert a spot-kick 16 times during his career, whilst netting 113 of the total 129 he has taken.
However, the striker’s penalty miss on Saturday evening was the first in the Der Klassiker between Bayern and Dortmund since 2012.
Bayern legend Arjen Robben was the last player to squander such an opportunity during a 1-0 Bundesliga defeat in April 2012.
Bayern held to draw by Dortmund
Konrad Laimer put the hosts in front in the 33rd minute shortly after Dortmund had a Jobe Bellingham goal disallowed for a foul.
Serhou Guirassy levelled on the hour mark, only for Kane to make up for his penalty miss by assisting Dayot Upamecano.
He headed the ball across the face of goal for the defender to pick up an eighth assist of the campaign.
Dortmund were close to their first defeat of the season, but saved by Fabio Silva with a minute to go thanks to his well-taken shot.
The historic rivals are level on 18 points with five wins and three draws, although Bayern are top of the Bundesliga on goal difference.
Bayern have lost only one of their last 18 competitive meetings with Dortmund, winning 13 and drawing four.
They are also unbeaten in their last 22 Bundesliga matches as leaders against the second-placed side, the league’s longest-ever run.
Kane had a helping hand in one of Bayern’s goals, but they could not hold onto their lead and had to settle for a draw in the derby Getty
Before kick-off, Kane was given a hero’s welcome by Bayern fans as they celebrated his Ballon d’Or win.
The England captain walked out onto the pitch and showcased the iconic golden ball to the crowd.
“I’m extremely proud to be a Bayern player,” he said. “I hope we win many more titles together.”
It was revealed on Friday that Kane won the 2026 Ballon d’Or ahead of Kylian Mbappe by just 28 points .
This is the fourth-closest voting gap in the prestigious award’s 70-year history.
Kane is now the fifth Englishman to win the award after Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen.
Kane showed off his Ballon d’Or trophy to the crowd before kick-off in Munich Getty

articles.headline: Serbia after Vucic: The winners are losing patience
keyFacts: Serbia's ruling party lost the October 25 election to the Student List, which won 53% of the vote.
The Student List unites diverse political groups seeking domestic reforms, while prosecutors investigate alleged electoral fraud under the previous administration.
Voting will be repeated in approximately 50 polling stations on Sunday before the new parliament convenes to form a government.
body: Aleksandar Vucic is accustomed to the spotlight. As Serbia's all-powerful president, loyal media outlets followed his every move for years. His TikTok outbursts led the evening news. But on October 25 he lost the election to the Student List, and since then, a lot has changed.

Vucic complained at a press conference, before fewer microphones than usual, that the winners were practising "revolutionary terror." He threatened: "If they continue to terrorize those who think differently – beatings, destruction and all the rest – and the state authorities do nothing, we will be forced to organize ourselves."
Vucic regards the immediate resignation of the general director of the Serbian state broadcaster RTS as an example of this "terror." Senior RTS editors have also been dismissed.

On Monday, a small group of protesters invaded the Informer TV station. Thousands of complaints have been lodged against Informer over the years for its demonization of Vucic critics. Now, journalists' associations are calling for its license to be revoked.
Tabloid media outlets loyal to Vucic have already changed their tone. Unlike Informer, they no longer refer to the Student List as "terrorists" and "mercenaries."
Old accusations against Vucic

The List, which emerged from the student revolt, is made up of professors, activists and artists. In the election on October 25, it won 53% of the vote, leaving Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) trailing with just 39%.

Since then, things have moved fast. In many cities, citizens peacefully removed portraits of Vucic from municipal buildings. The public prosecutor's office for organized crime has launched investigations, including into electoral fraud. A special commission is examining the work of the Higher Public Prosecutor's Office in Belgrade, which critics say did Vucic's bidding, and persecuted his opponents.

The accusations against him are old ones: that he and his system kept the media under tight control; that state contracts were only awarded to companies loyal to the regime; and that Vucic, his party, and the Serbian state had links to organized crime.

The catalyst for the revolt was the collapse, two years ago, of the concrete canopy on the newly renovated railway station in Novi Sad. Sixteen people died. The accident is believed to have happened as a result of poor workmanship and corruption in the awarding and execution of the renovation contract.
Those who were celebrating in the streets a few days ago are already growing impatient. The new parliament has not yet been convened, and the SNS still controls many levers of power.

"A society that was oppressed for so long by a party that acted like a feudal lord now, understandably, expects justice," Dejan Bursac from the Institute for Philosophy and Social Theory at Belgrade University told DW. "In this power vacuum, people are getting impatient."

Vucic and leading officials promise to be a strong opposition, and expect to make a quick comeback once "this lot" have ruined the country. But the majority of critics are calling for Vucic to be investigated and charged. "The SNS people are acting as if they had lost a local election somewhere in democratic Scandinavia, not as if they were part of a deeply corrupt and criminal regime," said Bursac.
How much damage can the old government do to the new one?

It's very common in Serbia for politicians to switch allegiance from one camp to another. They go where the power is. Even Vucic has admitted that many of his former comrades-in-arms are turning their backs on him. "We are going to see cases of people resigning or staying in the shadows, even putting themselves forward as informants for the next government," said Zlatko Minic from Transparency Serbia, an organization that monitors the work of governments.

The million-dollar question is: How much damage can the old government do to the new one? "There's still time for many officials to award contracts and create financial obligations for the agencies they run without necessarily committing a criminal offense," Minic warned.

However, those familiar with the situation said that for some time now the Student List has had contacts with officials in the police and administration opposed to Vucic's style of government. The winners of the election may now be able to prevent certain actions. On Wednesday, the List again demanded the resignations of leading officials in the police and judiciary. Whistleblowers were also asked to come forward if the outgoing government should try to "destroy documents."

In a symbolic move, Student List representatives held their first press conference in Pioneers Park in front of the parliament building. Vucic's followers fenced off the park in 2025, turning it into a pro-government encampment. According to investigative journalists, it also became a base for thugs and criminals who attacked anti-government demonstrators. The morning after the Student List's election win, its supporters went out with binbags and cleaned up the park.
No change in foreign policy

The victorious Student List unites left- and right-wingers, pro-European and pro-Russian forces. It is focussed on making changes in domestic politics, and wants to advance European Union accession talks by implementing real reforms. The List opposes sanctions on Russia and the recognition of Kosovo — positions that almost the entire population of Serbia agrees with.

"Our plan is to stabilize and develop the country, not to destabilize it with some abrupt change of course on foreign policy," Oliver Toskovic, a psychology professor and future member of parliament, told DW.

Toskovic said that, unlike under Vucic, the EU will not be misused as a "cover." Serbia's EU accession process recently stalled, with Vucic accusing "the West" of inciting a "color revolution" in Serbia.

"We are very dependent on Russia for energy. This is really a mistake of the previous government," Toskovic said. "But for that reason, sanctions right now would destabilize the country. And that would not be good for us or for the EU." How energy policy will develop under a Student List government is still unclear.

Where Vucic would frequently take aim at Kosovo, Croatia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina, leading representatives of the new List have promised better relationships with Serbia's neighbors and a reduction in tensions. On Kosovo, Ilija Srdanovic, the Student List's lead candidate, has said the party is open to dialog with the government in the Kosovar capital, Pristina. He has already spoken by phone with the prime minister of Croatia.

The electoral process is not yet over. On Sunday, November 1, the vote will be repeated in some 50 polling stations because there were irregularities first time around. Once these votes are counted, parliament can be convened. The formation of a government is expected to be quick, but for now the names of the prospective members have not been disclosed.
This article has been translated from German.

articles.headline: EA Offices Tagged With ‘Save Mass Effect’ Graffiti
keyFacts: Fans vandalized EA offices in Madrid with Save Mass Effect graffiti following the closure of BioWare.
Players previously bought a Times Square ad and started a petition that surpassed a quarter million signatures.
Politician Avi Lewis said stricter policies and federal funding should be used to protect and rebuild Canadian studios.
body: While evergreen to say that Mass Effect fans are having a rough go, itâs hard to imagine a worse couple of weeks. Earlier in the month, EA announced that they were closing BioWare, extinguishing any hope for a new entry along with it. Its most impassioned players have been incensed, to say the least, as one Reddit user stumbled across incidents of vandalism at one of the publisher’s offices.
“I stumbled upon the EA offices in Madrid as I was leaving a movie theater,” posted Reddit user Ok_Link9625, “saw this on the floor to the entrance and on the wall in front of the offices.”

Scrawled in spray paint in front of the Madrid officeâs front gate and along one wall reads “SAVE MASS EFFECT.” Itâs an escalation in efforts to salvage the beloved series from an unceremonious end. A few days earlier, a number of fans banded together to purchase a 15 second ad spot in Times Square. This is all coupled by a petition on Change demanding that EA continue developing games in the series, with or without BioWare’s involvement. As of this writing, the petition has amassed well over a quarter million signatures. The Spanish office itself largely works on various EA Sports titles.

Fans are ultimately torn between these escalating tactics, whether itâs a ‘bad look’ for the community or simply a wasted effort. While the righteous indignation is understandable, itâs unlikely any of this will reverse course at the company. Amid their controversial acquisition from a coalition of Saudi and Jared Kushner-affiliated firms, Jason Schreierâs sources told him EA decided to abandon Mass Effect in favor of safer Star Wars tie-ins, such as Battlefront 3. EA in general is not known for caretaking their legacy franchises or studios, with BioWare in particular at the center of numerous labor disputes.

Even if these campaigns did catch an executiveâs ear, it wouldnât change the fact that EA shuttered the studio responsible for the series. The key damage has been done. Avi Lewis, the recently elected leader of the Canadian federal New Democratic Party, said that stricter policy should be implemented to keep private equity from mulching Canadian studios, going so far to say that BioWare staff should receive federal funding to rebuild the studio for themselves.

articles.headline: All Status Effects in Queen’s Domain explained
keyFacts: Queen’s Domain features various status effects, such as Poison, Heavy, Weaker, Disease, Sticky, Binding, Paralysis, Azure Flame, and Magic Rot.
Each status effect applies a specific in-game modifier, like draining HP, reducing movement speed, or preventing attacks.
Most status effects resolve automatically over time, and players can also use dedicated cure items to heal instantly.
body: Queen’s Domain has a wide variety of different status effects you can apply to your enemies and vice versa. Each of these status effects applies a special in-game modifier.
In this guide, I will explain what each status effect means and how to know if you’re affected by one of them.
All Status Effects in Queen’s Domain
Image via Freshly Baked Games The following table has complete explanation of every Status Effect.

Status Effect Effects Poison Drains your HP slowly over time. You’ll have a purple mist on the top of your screen as an indicator. Heavy Your movement gets slower and your Power Regeneration also takes longer. Weaker Increases the amount of damage taken. Disease Reduces the damage you deal. It’s indicated by a black cloud on the screen. Sticky Stops you from using throwing weapons. You’ll find a spider’s web on your screen when this is active. Binding Stops you from using magic altogether, including all weapons with magical effects. It’s indicated by glowing green chains on the screen. Paralysis Prevents all types of movement and attacks. Azure Flame Drains your HP slowly due to burn. Look for blue flames on your screen. Magic Rot Once it builds up over time, it will drain your HP quickly. Thankfully for Queen’s Domain players, most Status Effects resolve automatically over time. You can also find dedicated cure items to instantly heal yourself from the negative effects, however.

body: Clashes erupt between police and protesters in Paris
